section_summary: This section contains U.S. diplomatic and military reporting on Japanese Communist activity from 1946 to July 1948. The documents discuss influence in newspapers and unions, party schools, alleged directives concerning power stations and repatriation vessels, opposition to American economic aid, and a proposed Far Eastern bloc. A Kyushu field report records local views on communist influence and economic conditions. Several despatches and enclosures appear twice.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Memorandum on Communist Activities in Press Circles in Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards an account of alleged Communist pressure on Japanese newspapers.
subfiles.summary: The adviser endorses the enclosed memorandum's account of intimidation and propaganda in press circles.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Communist Activities in Press Circles
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Examines newspaper management, union politics and alleged Communist efforts to influence the Japanese press.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum recounts postwar changes at the Mainichi and describes alleged Communist influence in newspaper employees' unions, especially at the Yomiuri. It alleges pressure on editors to print party material and fears that a purge of newspaper executives could help Communist organizers. It urges discreet handling of qualifications reviews and moral support for the Mainichi and Asahi.

subfiles.title: Report on Communist Party Schools in Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a military counterintelligence report on Communist Party schools.
subfiles.summary: Forwards five copies of the April 15 report.

subfiles.title: Note on Communist Party Schools
subfiles.about: Summarizes the party, labor union and people's school programs.
subfiles.summary: Highlights the programs' audiences, teaching methods, texts and estimated enrollment.

subfiles.title: Communist Party Schools, duplicated concluding leaf
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Counter-Intelligence
subfiles.about: Lists reported locations of Communist schools.
subfiles.summary: A duplicated concluding page of the report that begins again on page 11.

subfiles.title: Communist Party Schools
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Counter-Intelligence, General Headquarters
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese Communist educational programs for party members, union members and the public.
subfiles.summary: The report describes the Tokyo party school, its staff and curriculum, along with art, research, labor union and people's schools. It gives enrollment estimates and reports existing or planned schools in several prefectures. Pages 14 and 15 repeat the concluding material.

subfiles.title: Committee for Democratic Far Eastern Policy
subfiles.from: Intelligence Division, General Staff, U.S. Army
subfiles.to: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports an assessment of the Committee for Democratic Far Eastern Policy.
subfiles.summary: Calls the committee Communist dominated while qualifying several individual allegations and an unconfirmed meeting.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding a Japanese Diet member's New Year's card
subfiles.about: Relays a Diet member's concerns about Soviet influence and Communist agitation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Quotes a card alleging Soviet support for Japanese Communists, broadcasts from Moscow and disruption of industry.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Thomas
subfiles.from: Charles E. Bohlen for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds to concerns about Japanese Communist activity.
subfiles.summary: Bohlen calls Communists a small but disruptive minority and argues that economic recovery and higher living standards are needed to limit their influence.

subfiles.title: Further Japan Communist Party Directives Affecting the Occupation
subfiles.about: Forwards translations of two purported Communist Party directives.
subfiles.summary: Reports one local directive concerning power stations, inflation and intelligence gathering, and a national order opposing American economic assistance.

subfiles.title: Kurume Branch Directive No. 82
subfiles.from: Kurume Branch of the Japan Communist Party
subfiles.about: Sets out alleged plans involving power stations, covert party work and opposition to the occupation.
subfiles.summary: The translated compilation calls for cells in Kyushu power stations and describes plans to disrupt electricity, encourage inflation and gather information about American personnel. It also discusses the Northern Fraternity Association, covert members and a planned national meeting. The text includes directives and notes bearing several 1947 dates.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Order, Document No. 3: U.S. Policy Towards Japan
subfiles.about: Urges opposition to proposed American credit and economic assistance.
subfiles.summary: Portrays U.S. aid as economic colonization and instructs regional committees to turn the credit issue toward a people's revolution.

subfiles.title: Correction to Despatch No. 153
subfiles.about: Corrects a phrase in the March 9 despatch.
subfiles.summary: Changes “Civil Information” to “Civil Intelligence.”

subfiles.title: Further Japan Communist Party Directives Affecting the Occupation, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the despatch on two purported Communist directives.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of pages 20–21, with a fuller reading of the passage corrected by the airgram.

subfiles.title: Kurume Branch Directive No. 82, second copy
subfiles.from: Kurume Branch of the Japan Communist Party
subfiles.about: Repeats the translated material on power stations and covert Communist activity.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of pages 22–25.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Order, Document No. 3, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the order opposing American economic assistance.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of pages 26–27.

subfiles.title: Correction to Despatch No. 153, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the correction to the March 9 despatch.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of page 28.

subfiles.title: Reported Japanese Communist Party Espionage on Japanese Repatriation Vessels
subfiles.about: Forwards an intelligence summary of an alleged party order concerning repatriation vessels.
subfiles.summary: Describes instructions to investigate demobilization officials and interfere with their work.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Order, Document No. 14
subfiles.doc_type: military intelligence summary and translated order
subfiles.about: Presents a translated directive to Communist fractions in seamen's unions.
subfiles.summary: The order directs party members aboard repatriation ships to observe demobilization officials, obstruct investigations and report details of sympathetic senior ship personnel.

subfiles.title: Report of Formation of Far Eastern Block
subfiles.about: Forwards an intelligence account of a proposed Communist Far Eastern bloc.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Party Order No. 15 and its claims about regional coordination and labor action.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Order, Document No. 15
subfiles.doc_type: military intelligence summary and translated order
subfiles.from: Military Intelligence Section, Far East Command
subfiles.about: Translates an alleged March 19 party order about forming a Far Eastern bloc.
subfiles.summary: The order links Japanese Communist labor activity to a proposed regional bloc and names a preparation committee led by Tokuda Kyuichi.

subfiles.title: Communist Activities in Kyushu
subfiles.about: Forwards Lawrence's field memorandum on Communist activity in four Kyushu prefectures.
subfiles.summary: The despatch highlights local views that economic aid is needed to limit Communist influence. It notes changes in labor and agricultural areas, the influence of a small organized party, and demand for democratic labor education.

subfiles.title: Communist Activities in Kyushu
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports interviews with Japanese leaders and military government officials across Kyushu.
subfiles.summary: Lawrence finds that Communist influence persists despite setbacks in some unions and may be increasing in agricultural areas. Interviewees stress the party's organization, economic hardship and the need for American aid and labor education. The memorandum also discusses students, repatriates, surveillance of party members and alleged funding through smuggled goods.

subfiles.title: Communist Activities in Kyushu, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the cover despatch forwarding Lawrence's Kyushu memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of pages 45–46.

subfiles.title: Soviet press report of attempted assassination of Tokuda
subfiles.about: Reports a Soviet press item on an alleged attempt to assassinate the Japanese Communist Party secretary general.
subfiles.summary: Says Soviet press echoed a Reuters report of an attempted assassination of Tokuda.
